note: Directives for the Allied seat of the 39 days of Guadalcanal, 7 August to 14 September 1942. Written for the game in its own words: these are not historical documents and quote none. Each gives the situation as the commander above has it and the mission with its purpose, and nothing the commander can find out for himself: what the enemy has, what is coming and what cannot be replaced are read elsewhere on the table. Decision 0157.

directives.from: Commander in Chief, U.S. Pacific Fleet
directives.to: Commander, South Pacific Area and South Pacific Force
directives.subject: Tulagi and Lunga Point

parts.heading: 1. Situation
text: Japanese forces occupy Tulagi. An airfield is reported under construction at Lunga Point, Guadalcanal. Aircraft operating from that field would threaten communications with Australia.

parts.heading: 2. Mission
text: Seize and hold Tulagi and the airfield at Lunga Point, to safeguard communications with Australia.

parts.heading: 3. Execution
text: Employ the forces assigned to your command as you judge necessary. The method is yours.
Further direction will follow as the situation requires.

directives.from: Commander in Chief, U.S. Pacific Fleet
directives.to: Commander, South Pacific Area and South Pacific Force
directives.subject: Lunga Point

parts.heading: 1. Situation
text: Lunga Point is in your hands. The enemy is expected to contest it by sea and by air from Rabaul, and to land troops on Guadalcanal. His carriers are reported likely to come south in support.

parts.heading: 2. Mission
text: Hold Lunga Point and Tulagi. Bring the airfield into operation and keep it in operation, to deny the enemy the southern Solomons.

parts.heading: 3. Execution
text: Further direction will follow as the situation requires.
